strengths: Conditional summary graphs provide a useful, compact representation of changing interactions. Under the source-specific state assumption, representing K graphs instead of enumerating K^N regimes is a meaningful contribution.

SDCI is a well-motivated extension of ACD/NRI that combines shared interaction functions with local discrete states. The distinction between observed, determined, and recurrent states clarifies the problem, and the paper acknowledges unresolved estimator consistency and state-number selection.

The experiments provide encouraging evidence: nearly perfect structure recovery in the fixed-graph particle setting, improved GRN F1 scores, and better NBA forecasting than VRNN and NRI-MPM. The appendices provide substantial architecture, training, and simulation details.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.3 is false under the permitted aggregation functions. Consider scalar messages f0=0, f1(a,b)=a, f2(a,b)=π−a, and g(b,{h})=b+Σ sin(h). Assumptions (a2.1–a2.2) hold almost everywhere, but types 1 and 2 produce identical contributions because sin(a)=sin(π−a). Changing selected edge labels therefore preserves the observational distribution without requiring a single global label permutation; distinct on/off outgoing patterns can still satisfy (a1). Corollary A.8 incorrectly assumes that permutation invariance makes aggregation derivatives identical across edges and independent of states. Stronger aggregation assumptions and a corrected proof are needed for this central guarantee.

Theorem A.6 applies Gaussian-mixture identifiability in Eq. (35) without establishing positive weights for all U components. In the explicitly targeted deterministic-state setting, conditioning on the observed history can leave only one active component, so U and all component distributions cannot be identified by this argument. Moreover, the assumptions allow unvisited states whose structures can be changed without affecting observations. Consequently, identification of the number of states and the complete graph collection is unsupported without additional coverage conditions.

The claim of exact state inference in Section 3.3 and Appendix B.2 is incorrect for the softmax categorical model in Eq. (14). Future observations generally inform s_t, so p(s_t|x_1:T,W) is not simply p(s_t|x_t). Shared source states also induce dependencies between target observations after marginalization, invalidating the factorization in Eq. (56). Setting the variational distribution equal to the state prior can provide an approximation, but it does not establish the claimed exact inference or O(NK) likelihood marginalization. Truly deterministic point-mass states require separate treatment.

The comparisons do not convincingly isolate the advantage over alternative approaches to changing causal structure. Most particle baselines assume a fixed graph; the cited regime-switching approaches are not evaluated there. R-PCMCI appears only in the GRN experiment, using defaults after tuning encountered short-sequence errors. The challenging recurrent, variable-graph setting is evaluated only at three and five variables and already shows substantial degradation.

Important evaluation details are missing: graph threshold selection, alignment of latent state and edge-type permutations, seed counts, and definitions of plotted error bars. Table 1 provides no uncertainty, while SDCI and Rhino have almost identical AUROC (0.936 versus 0.933) despite very different F1 scores. Appendix D.2 also needs to clarify its micro-F1 calculation: averaging over both binary classes yields accuracy and can obscure performance on sparse positive edges. These omissions make the magnitude and robustness of the reported advantage difficult to assess.

The application claims exceed the validation. GRN results concern one simulated 49-gene network using longitudinal measurements of the same cells, which Appendix C.2 acknowledges are generally unavailable in sequencing experiments. NBA evaluates forecasting conditioned on ball features and offers qualitative graph interpretations without causal ground truth; its improvement over ACD is slight. These experiments do not establish reliable causal recovery in realistic applications, leaving insufficient empirical support to compensate for the theoretical and inference problems.
